bound: a collision is a property of one key under one reading of the corpus: two values that normalise apart and each resolve to a file.  A value that resolves to no file, or to many, is published under its own state and is never counted as one identified file, so the headline under-reports rather than invents.  The published E350/E353/E377 faces are read, never rebuilt or rewritten.  Several of the consuming faces are themselves keying studies (E380/E381 report the same key set), so a consumption count is not a claim that many independent readers rely on the merge.

summary.consumer_test: a quoted key is 'consumed as one face' only when it sits in a list with at least one other key; a key inside a sentence is a mention and is reported separately in consumer_rows
summary.keying_scope: the population is load bindings AND dump sinks, the union the published key set is built from; json.dump rows keep the published helper's 'target must be a Name' condition so a writer-only key is counted exactly when E350 counts it
summary.normalisation: values are compared after the same replace('\\','/').strip('./') the key helper applies, so two spellings of one file never count as a collision
summary.resolution: a folded value is resolved by suffix against one index of the tree (a value with exactly one hit is an identified file; a value with two or more hits is published as ambiguous and never counted as one file); absolute values are tested on disk directly
